thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV2 — Multiple customers reporting 502/525s to api.redwood-inference.com (TLS handshake failures) — paging on-call
Alice Nguyen: seeing a flood of errors in the hosted-api ingest graph around 07:34 UTC. 525s and TLS handshake errors from edge.
Ben Patel: confirmed. synthetic checks show curl to https://api.redwood-inference.com returns "SSL connect error" intermittently. digging.
Carla Ruiz: I can repro from my laptop: `curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.com` -> `* SSL: error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert protocol version` then handshake abort.
Dave Kim: are DNS A records resolving for the domain? running `dig api.redwood-inference.com +short`
Alice Nguyen: dig returned nothing from my end (us-west). from us-east gave the old Cloudflare IPs. looks inconsistent.
Erin O'Connor: support queue spiking, customers reporting model timeouts and failed requests. triaging incoming tickets.
Maddy Johnson: checking Dedicated clusters — telemetry shows no handshake errors from internal VPC endpoints (dedicated.private.redwood). Looks isolated to public API via Cloudflare.
Ben Patel: hitting Cloudflare 525/526 codes which indicates origin handshake or TLS to edge problem OR Cloudflare edge-to-origin. But DNS flakiness suggests edge routing issues too.
Cloudflare Status Bot: https://status.cloudflare.com/incident/xyz — "Partial service disruption affecting TLS handshakes and DNS propagation in the US West region" (posted 07:38 UTC).
Alice Nguyen: good find. Is this purely an edge outage or are we seeing origin certificate mismatch? origin certs still valid. `openssl s_client -connect origin-internal.redwood-inference:443` returns cert chain OK from our origin.
Carla Ruiz: looks like Cloudflare edge is failing to complete TLS with clients. Some connections succeed to certain POPs, others fail. The mixed dig results suggest DNS updates or BGP propagation issues at CF.
Ben Patel: realtime mitigation options: 1) failover to alternate hostname (api-backup.redwood-inference.com) pointed at different provider; 2) instruct clients to use direct origin IPs (not ideal); 3) contact CF support for edge rollback.
Dave Kim: we do have an alternate vanity hostname (api-alt.redwood-inference.com) that was used during last year's migration but it routes through the same CF setup. Not helpful.
Maddy Johnson: do we have a non-CF CDN / direct path? private customers can use dedicated endpoints, public traffic mostly goes through CF.
Erin O'Connor: customer-facing comms: we need a status page update ASAP. spike in errors across top 10 customers (list sent to eng lead).
Alice Nguyen: action: I'll open an urgent ticket with Cloudflare and request rollback to previous edge config + confirm DNS propagation status. Ben, start collecting curl/wire traces to attach.
Ben Patel: attaching sample curl output and tcpdump extract (pasted below) for CF: ```
* Connected to api.redwood-inference.com (104.18.12.34) port 443
* ALPN, offering h2
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2)
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS alert, handshake failure (552)
* curl: (35) error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert protocol version
```
Carla Ruiz: dig traces: `dig @8.8.8.8 api.redwood-inference.com +short` -> `104.18.12.34` then immediately `; Connection timed out; no servers could be reached` from another region. Cloudflare's anycast seems partially degraded.
Cloudflare Status Bot: Real-time update: "Investigating — an edge routing issue affecting TLS termination in multiple POPs" (07:46 UTC).
Maddy Johnson: must quantify customer impact. Alice, can you pull error rates by product? Are embeddings/streaming equally affected?
Alice Nguyen: embeddings calls largely failing (75% errors) in us-west, streaming sessions drop during initial handshake. So user-visible impact: inability to start or complete generation requests.
Erin O'Connor: support note draft: "We're seeing degraded availability to our public API in select regions due to a third-party network issue. Our teams are actively working with the CDN provider and monitoring customer impact. We'll post updates every 30 minutes." Thoughts?
Ben Patel: technical note to CF: include `tcpdump` traces, `curl -v` logs, `dig +trace` output, timestamps, ASN details. Also ask if they have any edge config changes at that time.
Dave Kim: while CF works it, we can prepare an emergency route: add a short-lived CNAME that points to a non-CF provider and update DNS TTL low (but propagation may be slow). Alternatively, enable our failover domain with direct IPs in DNS for affected customers via support docs.
Carla Ruiz: DNS TTLs are 60s for the API record, so in theory switches could propagate quickly; but if CF anycast is blackholing traffic, changing CNAME might not help for clients bound to a bad POP.
Alice Nguyen: I'm on the CF call now (joining). They confirm two POPs had misconfigured TLS frontends after a config push. Their rollback is in progress. ETA initial mitigation 10–15 minutes.
Cloudflare Status Bot: Update: "Rollback started, mitigation expected within 15 minutes" (07:54 UTC).
Maddy Johnson: great. Start cooling down incident comms once error rate drops below 5% for 10 minutes.
Erin O'Connor: support outreach: pinged top 5 impacted customers with current status + workaround (use dedicated endpoints or try alt region).
Ben Patel: observed partial recovery at 08:02 UTC. some POPs now completing TLS. Errors down from 78% -> 32%. Still noisy.
Alice Nguyen: CF team applied rollback. They say propagation orthogonally impacted; still monitoring.
Carla Ruiz: continuing to see handshake failures from a slice of clients in us-west-2. I recommend we temporarily enable HTTP -> HTTPS redirect tests offload to minimize handshakes? Not sure that'll help.
Dave Kim: don't disable HTTPS globally. Could we temporarily increase retry/backoff on client SDKs to avoid immediate failures? That is more of a client SDK change which is riskier but low-touch if we flip a runtime flag.
Maddy Johnson: On-call handoff in 30 minutes to Ben. I'll prepare runbook summary.
Alice Nguyen: CF final update: "Rollback complete, service stable in most regions. Monitoring for residual errors." (08:18 UTC).
Ben Patel: error rate back to ~3% by 08:21 UTC. I'm seeing clean digs and successful TLS handshakes from all test POPs.
Erin O'Connor: support: tickets decreasing, customers acknowledging restored service. posting finished incident note draft to #incidents-docs.
Carla Ruiz: follow-up items: 1) validate edge config pinning for critical hostnames, 2) run extended synthetic probes across all POPs, 3) add automated alerting on selective-POP TLS handshake failures (not just 5xx percent).
Dave Kim: cc: infra — add Cloudflare tenant audit for config pushes during that window, request CF postmortem.
Maddy Johnson: handing off to Ben Patel (on-call) — details in runbook: https://internal/docs/incidents/1769123456 (will post summary and timeline).
Ben Patel: accepting handoff — I'll own the postmortem and coordinate CF follow-up. final update: incident declared RESOLVED at 08:33 UTC but with follow-ups required. Thanks all for quick triage. :white_check_mark:
Alice Nguyen: thanks team. I'll push the status page final update and close the oncall ticket.
Erin O'Connor: closing support bridge. customers notified of restoration and followups.
incident-bot: Incident thread closed by Ben Patel (RESOLVED).
